itinerary.cal: Best mid-July through September after the Mountaineer Creek approach and ridge lose their early-season snow and ice.

days.note: Hike via the Colchuck Lake trail and the Mountaineer Creek boot path (or over Longs Pass, Ingalls Creek, and the Sherpa-Argonaut col from the south), then climb steep talus and heather to a flat, sandy ledge just below the ridge crest near the notch.
days.title: Approach to high bivy
days.objective: Reach the class 2 ledge below the North Ridge crest (~7,800 ft)

days.note: The route alternates class 4 scrambling with several roped pitches up to 5.8 (a chimney and blocky cracks), reaching the summit in about 3 hours from the bivy. Descend with a short rappel off the summit, downclimb a class 3 gully, traverse to the Sherpa-Argonaut saddle, and descend loose terrain back to treeline and the trailhead — the standard route.
days.title: Climb North Ridge, descend to Mountaineer Creek side

schedule.label: Climb the 5.7-5.8 pitches
schedule.detail: Chimney and cracks with some loose blocks

schedule.label: Summit
schedule.detail: About 3 hours after leaving the bivy

schedule.label: Rappel off the summit
schedule.detail: ~30 ft rappel from an anchor west of the top

schedule.label: Downclimb and traverse
schedule.detail: Class 3 gully, then across to the Sherpa-Argonaut saddle

schedule.label: Reach treeline / trailhead
schedule.detail: Descend loose terrain and hike out

days.objective: Climb the 5.8 North Ridge and descend via the Sherpa-Argonaut saddle

itinerary.totalNote: A 2-day trip, roughly 13.5 miles and ~5,000 ft gain round trip; this is Sherpa's most serious route (5.8, loose rock) so parties move deliberately.
